question: Is Gaussian lifecycle a new, exploitable 3DGS training-optimization dimension beyond visibility?
decision_rule: PROMISING iff C1 AND C2 AND C3; DROP if lifecycle highly overlaps visibility OR headroom<10%. No override.

C1_stable_lifecycle_pattern.evidence: 3-stage NEW/MATURE/INACTIVE discovered by unsupervised GMM (BIC k=4-5 fine structure) on all 3 scenes; operational 3-stage labeling stable across TV/TA thresholds; transition matrix diagonally dominant (persistence>0.6).

C2_lifecycle_not_visibility.evidence: corr(stage,vis_frac) max 0.41 (not deterministic); INACTIVE sometimes visible (always-invisible fraction 0.01-0.27); additional headroom 12.84% comes from VISIBLE mature gaussians that VOS updates every iter.

C3_headroom_ge_10pct.evidence: additional_safe_skip_headroom=12.84% pooled (freq=2), per-scene room 12.8% / bicycle 10.6% / garden 15.7%; robust 12.6-14.5% across TV/TA.

headroom_decomposition.dominant_lever: MATURE frequency reduction (INACTIVE-only at freq=1 is 0.48%)

caveats: Headroom is a theoretical oracle assuming mature-Gaussian updates can be halved without quality loss; GLM1 must validate with a quality gate.
Dominant lever is MATURE frequency reduction; if quality-unsafe, realized headroom collapses toward the INACTIVE-only 0.48%.
Effect is scene-dependent (garden 15.7% > room 12.8% > bicycle 10.6%); all three pass the 10% gate at freq=2.
Frozen-C0 run-to-run nondeterminism (~1% N spread) applies; oracle uses per-scene sampled-iteration visibility, ratio is seed-42 frozen.
paper_decision: GLM0_PROMISING -> enter GLM1: lifecycle-aware optimizer scheduling (quality-gated mature-frequency reduction on top of VOS visibility baseline).
